title: The Spire of Caerlum
premise: Xanthe Nystrom, a bone-carver who hears the dead through the relics she carves, has survived three years in Caerlum by keeping her gift small and secret in a city where magic is outlawed. When a mute child arrives at her door speaking a language older than any kingdom, Xanthe discovers the child carries a fragment of the true king's soul — stolen and bound beneath the Spire by the regent, whose crown is slowly being worn from the inside by something ancient called the Hollow King. Guided by the dead who remember what was buried, Xanthe must descend the Spire to unbind the king before the Hollow King finishes wearing him. She succeeds at terrible cost: the child's fragment returns to its body, but Xanthe's own hearing of the dead is spent as payment, leaving her deaf to ghosts yet finally belonging among the living.
about_author: Juniper Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former museum conservator who spent years restoring medieval bone reliquaries before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about grief, craft, and the stubborn persistence of the forgotten.

chapters.title: The Quiet Trade
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. We meet her selling carved charms that whisper comfort to buyers, hiding her gift from Caerlum's Wardens who burn magic-workers. A routine sale goes wrong when a charm screams with a warning she can't parse. Emotional beat: loneliness and vigilance; the cost of staying small.

chapters.title: A Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. On a rain-lashed night, a child appears speaking a language predating kingdoms — and Xanthe's bones answer it, resonating without being carved. The child cannot speak anything else and clutches a broken crown-shaped amulet. Emotional beat: fear giving way to reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: What the Bones Remember
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Carving into an old relic, Xanthe contacts a dead archivist who reveals the child carries a fragment of the true king's soul, hidden during the regency. The Wardens raid her street hunting 'resonance.' Emotional beat: revelation and the first taste of open danger.

chapters.title: The Regent's Smile
chapters.summary: Regent Aldous Vane's POV. Vane feels the Hollow King stirring inside his mind, promising power for obedience. He orders the city sealed to find the escaped fragment. Emotional beat: chilling intimacy with villainy — a man rationalizing his own consumption.

chapters.title: Underground of Saints
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Following the dead archivist's directions, Xanthe and the child flee into catacombs beneath Caerlum, meeting a hidden community of outlawed magic-keepers who recognize the child's language. Emotional beat: tentative belonging — the first people who don't flinch at her gift.

chapters.title: The Price List
chapters.summary: Keeper Maren's POV. The keepers explain the unbinding rite: it requires a soul-hearing guide, and every unbinding takes something permanent from the one who performs it. Xanthe conceals that she already knows what hers will cost. Emotional beat: dread braided with resolve.

chapters.title: Wardens at the Gate
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, Xanthe and Warden-Captain Ilsa Renn. The keepers' sanctuary is betrayed; Ilsa, ordered to burn children, hesitates when the amulet resonates against her own family's bones. The group escapes through a collapsing passage. Emotional beat: moral fracture inside the machine of law.

chapters.title: The Ascent
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The party climbs the Spire itself, passing floors of bound dead who beg Xanthe to listen — each listening costing her warmth, memory edges, color. The Hollow King speaks to her directly, offering her the dead back forever. Emotional beat: temptation at maximum pressure.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, climax. At the crown chamber, Xanthe performs the rite as Vane fights his own possessor from within. She pours her hearing of the dead into the unbinding; the true king's soul reunites with the child's fragment, and the Hollow King, unworn, unravels. Vane dies human. Emotional beat: sacrifice made real, not noble-feeling but costly.

chapters.title: After the Silence
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, resolution. Weeks later, Caerlum debates its laws while the restored young king learns to rule. Xanthe, deaf to ghosts now, carves a plain wooden toy instead of a charm — and finds the living enough. The keepers call her family. Emotional beat: quiet belonging earned through loss.
